# Kammakkhandhaka (Kd 11)
**ID:** Kd 11
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kammakkhandhaka* is the opening chapter of the *Cullavagga* within the Khandhaka division of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [Hazra 1994; Williams 2005]. It provides detailed legal regulations governing the validity, enactment, offender duties, and eventual revocation of formal disciplinary procedures (*kamma*) initiated by the Saṅgha against offending monks [SuttaCentral; Vinayamukha 1983]. These disciplinary proceedings include censure or rebuke (*tajjanīyakamma*), subordination or guidance (*nissayakamma*), banishment from a locality (*pabbājanīyakamma*), reconciliation with laypersons (*paṭisāraṇīyakamma*), and suspension (*ukkhepanīyakamma*), the latter imposed for offences such as refusing to acknowledge or atone for an offence or refusing to renounce harmful views [Vinayamukha 1983; Sung 1999]. A monk undergoing such sanctions loses particular monastic privileges and may be prohibited from communal fellowship (*sambhoga*), requiring strict adherence to prescribed modes of conduct until formal restoration to full standing [Vinayamukha 1983; Banerjee 1979; Williams 2005].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral identify full parallels across other Vinaya lineages under the title *Pāṇḍulohitakavastu* (extant in Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese Mūlasarvāstivāda texts, as well as Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Mahīśāsaka Vinayas) [SuttaCentral; Banerjee 1979; Prebish 1994]. Furthermore, its core cluster of formal proceedings corresponds to disciplinary topics in the first and second *vargas* of the Mahāsāmghika Vinaya [Sung 1999]. SuttaCentral also notes passage-level parallels with AN 8.89, MN 22, the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (Ss 13 and Pc 68), and Kd 15 [SuttaCentral]. In agreement with these identifications, DharmaNexus matches Kd 11 externally with the Sanskrit *Pāṇḍulohitakavastu* and Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (D0001-3), as well as the Tibetan *Ekottarakarmaśataka* [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus detects extensive text reuse with other legal sections of the Vinaya, most notably the *Campeyyakkhandhaka* (Kd 9), the *Samathakkhandhaka* (Kd 14), the *Upālipañcaka* (Pvr 17), the *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), the *Ekuttarikanaya* (Pvr 7), and the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
